newsitem.title: USA: Flooding in N. Carolina leaves most crops unharmed.
newsitem.headline: Flooding in N. Carolina leaves most crops unharmed.

text.p: Flooding and heavy rains caused by the remnants of Hurricane Danny on Wednesday were expected to cause only isolated damage to corn, soybean and cotton crops in North Carolina, a state government official said Thursday.
"There will be damage reports, but in isolated areas only," said Jeff Chaffin, with the state's Agricultural Statistics Service. "This rain is more more helpful than harmful on a statewide basis."
Flooding, extremely heavy rains and high winds were reported in southwestern and central North Carolina, where much of the state's crops are grown.

The city of Charlotte, which received the brunt of the rains, reported 8.31 inches of rain this week, most of it in the past 48 hours, according to data from Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass.
It was still raining on Thursday, so farmers had not yet had a chance to fully assess crop damage caused by the storm, Chaffin said.
Little damage from standing water was expected because fields were very short of moisture before the storm and high temperatures were expected beginning Friday, Chaffin said.
"Basically, we have a heat wave coming right behind the storm, so even if a field has standing water, it's not going to be standing for long," he said.
The storm was not expected to have any impact on the state's overall yields, Chaffin said.
